topics: 🏘️ Four Domains of Shabbat — private, public, karmelit, and the exempt domain, defined
🔍 Chasing a Precedent — can carrying through the colonnade, an exempt domain, still create liability?
🎯 Ben Azzai's Concession — carrying by hand is exempt, but throwing through the colonnade is not
🚪 The Threshold's Two Faces — open door, locked door, and a fully independent domain
🚧 Posts and Beams — why Rabbi Yehuda's makeshift private domain in the public street is rejected

overview.title: 📖 Overview: Mapping Out the Domains of Shabbat
overview.subtitle: Shabbat 6a–6b
overview.hebrewSource: אַרְבַּע רְשׁוּיוֹת לַשַּׁבָּת: רְשׁוּת הַיָּחִיד, וּרְשׁוּת הָרַבִּים, וְכַרְמְלִית, וּמְקוֹם פְּטוּר
overview.label: The scene:
overview.text: Daf 6 opens by resolving the previous daf's unfinished question: can one be liable for carrying an object out through a colonnade — an exempt domain — the way one is liable for carrying through the ordinary midpoint of a public domain? After testing several precedents and refining Rabbi Eliezer ben Ya'akov's ruling about the 'sides' of the public domain, the Gemara settles the matter and clarifies that ben Azzai's exemption applies only to carrying by hand, not to throwing. The Gemara then cites the Tosefta's foundational map of the four domains of Shabbat law — private domain, public domain, karmelit, and exempt domain — working through their definitions, the special status of thresholds, and why Rabbi Yehuda's proposal to fence off part of a public street with posts and beams is firmly rejected.

slides.title: 🏘️ Four Domains of Shabbat
slides.subtitle: The Tosefta's foundational map of where carrying is, and isn't, prohibited by Torah law
rows: A main street, a large plaza, alleyways open on both ends
Torah-level liability for transfer to/from a private domain: sin-offering if unwitting, karet or stoning if intentional
A ditch 10 handbreadths deep and 4 wide; a fence 10 high and 4 wide
Same Torah-level liability for improper transfer to/from the public domain
A sea, a valley, a colonnade — frequented by the public, but with no proper partitions
Carrying beyond 4 cubits, or to/from RH or RY, is only rabbinically prohibited
An area under 4×4 handbreadths, such as many thresholds
No prohibition at all — except one may not relay an object between RH and RY through it

callout.label: Note:
callout.text: Shared courtyards and alleyways not open at both ends carry the same restriction as a karmelit, unless the residents join them with an eiruv into a single legal domain.

slides.title: 🔍 Chasing a Precedent Through the Colonnade
slides.subtitle: Can carrying an object through an exempt domain still trigger liability?

steps.content: 1️⃣ First try: like carrying across the public domain generally — an in-between point is exempt only because the labor isn't finished. Rejected: that midpoint is still a potential place of LIABILITY, while the colonnade is an absolute exempt zone

2️⃣ Second try: like carrying exactly four cubits — a midpoint is exempt only for THIS person, but a place of liability for the world at large. Rejected: the colonnade is exempt for everyone, with no exceptions
3️⃣ Third try: like carrying via the narrow 'sides' of the public domain, where the multitudes don't gather — a lesser status within the same physical domain

4️⃣ Rav Acha's refinement: this comparison to Rabbi Eliezer ben Ya'akov's 'sides of the public domain' works only where there are no boundary stakes (חִיפּוּפֵי) — precisely then it parallels the colonnade

callout.label: Result:
callout.text: One who carries from a store through the colonnade to the plaza is liable — the sides-of-the-public-domain precedent, properly qualified, holds.

slides.title: 🎯 Ben Azzai's Concession on Throwing
slides.subtitle: Walking through an exempt domain is different from an unbroken throw

nodes.content: ❓ Does ben Azzai's exemption for carrying an object BY HAND through the colonnade also apply to one who THROWS it across?

columns.label: Carrying by walking
columns.content: EXEMPT, according to ben Azzai — each step is treated as if he came to a stop, so he 'rests' inside the colonnade itself

columns.label: Throwing or extending the hand
columns.content: LIABLE, even according to ben Azzai — the object's flight, or the outstretched arm, is uninterrupted; there is no stopping point along the way

nodes.content: ✅ Rabbi Yochanan: ben Azzai concedes on throwing; a baraita confirms the identical distinction for מוֹצִיא, מַכְנִיס, מוֹשִׁיט, and זוֹרֵק

callout.label: The dividing line:
callout.text: Walking involves repeated, momentary 'placements'; throwing and reaching do not — that is what separates ben Azzai's exemption from his liability.

slides.title: 🚪 The Threshold's Two Faces
slides.subtitle: Acherim's ruling on a threshold's shifting legal status
rows: Subsumed within the house — treated as a private domain
Not subsumed within the house — treated as a public domain
10 handbreadths high and 4 wide, regardless of the door
An independent domain in its own right, a full private domain

callout.label: Connects back to 2a:
callout.text: This is the same threshold from the Tosefta's example of an exempt domain — one may stand there and take from, or give to, either side, but never relay an object directly between the private and public sides.

slides.title: 🚧 Posts and Beams: A Private Domain Carved Out of the Street?
slides.subtitle: Why the Tosefta insists on calling the real private domain 'full-fledged'

lines.speaker: R' Yehuda
lines.text: One who has two houses on opposite sides of a public street may set posts (לֶחִי) on each side, or a beam (קוֹרָה) spanning across — and then carry freely in the space between, as though it were a private domain.

lines.speaker: Rabbis
lines.text: One may not fashion an eiruv of the public domain in that way! Only genuine partitions create a private domain.

lines.speaker: Gemara
lines.text: Then why does the Tosefta stress 'זוֹ הִיא רְשׁוּת הַיָּחִיד גְּמוּרָה' — this is a FULL-FLEDGED private domain? What is the extra word 'full-fledged' excluding?

lines.speaker: Gemara
lines.text: Precisely Rabbi Yehuda's posts-and-beam construction — lest you think the Rabbis merely forbid carrying there, but would still treat it as a private domain for the more severe prohibition of throwing an object into it. 'Full-fledged' teaches: no, the Rabbis reject it as a private domain entirely.

callout.label: Parallel exclusion:
callout.text: The identical emphasis for the public domain excludes Rabbi Yehuda's separate ruling that a path passing through pilgrimage wells must be diverted — the Tosefta insists only its own listed examples count as a full public domain.

summary.principle: The four domains of Shabbat — public, private, karmelit, and exempt — are fixed categories with fixed rules; carrying through an exempt domain like a colonnade can still create liability under the right precedent, but only by walking, not by an uninterrupted throw, and no rabbinic construction of posts and beams can convert a public street into a true private domain.

flowSteps.content: 🏘️ Tosefta: four domains — public, private, karmelit, and exempt — each with its own carrying rule
🔍 Can carrying through the colonnade (exempt domain) still trigger liability? Rav Acha: yes, when it parallels the unstaked 'sides of the public domain'
🎯 Ben Azzai exempts carrying BY HAND through the colonnade, but concedes liability for THROWING through it

columns.content: 🚪 A threshold's status shifts with the door — open (inside), locked (outside), or 10×4 (independent)
🚧 Rabbi Yehuda's posts-and-beam street enclosure is rejected outright by the Rabbis

flowSteps.content: 🎓 Key Principle: only genuine partitions create a private domain — rabbinic markers and momentary pauses cannot substitute for them

quiz.q: According to the Tosefta, what are the four domains relevant to the halakhot of Shabbat?
o: Home, synagogue, marketplace, and field
Private domain, public domain, karmelit, and exempt domain
Temple, city, wilderness, and sea
Weekday, Shabbat, festival, and Yom Kippur
quiz.e: The Tosefta lists רְשׁוּת הַיָּחִיד (private domain), רְשׁוּת הָרַבִּים (public domain), כַּרְמְלִית (karmelit), and מְקוֹם פְּטוּר (exempt domain) as the four categories.

quiz.q: What level of liability applies to carrying within, or to and from, a karmelit?
o: The same as the public domain — sin-offering, karet, or stoning
None at all — a karmelit is treated exactly like an exempt domain
Only rabbinic prohibition, with no Torah-level liability
Liability only on Yom Kippur
quiz.e: A karmelit is a rabbinic construct: carrying beyond four cubits within it, or transferring to or from it, is prohibited only by rabbinic decree, not by Torah law.

quiz.q: According to Rav Acha, when does the ruling about the 'sides of the public domain' (Rabbi Eliezer ben Ya'akov's view) serve as a valid precedent for liability when carrying through the colonnade?
o: Only on Friday afternoon
Specifically where there are no boundary stakes (חִיפּוּפֵי) separating the sides from the actual public domain
Only when the colonnade has a roof
Never — the comparison always fails
quiz.e: Rav Acha qualifies the comparison: Rabbi Eliezer ben Ya'akov's ruling that the sides are like the public domain applies only where there are no stakes, and it is specifically that case which parallels the colonnade.

quiz.q: According to Rabbi Yochanan, does ben Azzai's exemption for carrying through the colonnade by hand also apply to throwing an object through it?
o: Yes, ben Azzai exempts both equally
No — ben Azzai concedes that throwing or extending a hand through the colonnade is liable, since the motion is uninterrupted
Ben Azzai never discusses throwing
Throwing is always exempt regardless of ben Azzai's opinion
quiz.e: Ben Azzai's exemption relies on walking being treated as a series of momentary stops; a throw or an extended hand has no such interruption, so even ben Azzai agrees one is liable.

quiz.q: Why does the Tosefta emphasize that the true private domain is 'גְּמוּרָה' (full-fledged)?
o: To indicate that it must be built of stone
To exclude Rabbi Yehuda's proposal that posts and a beam can turn part of a public street into a private domain, even for the graver prohibition of throwing into it
To show that only priests may carry there
To clarify that it applies only on festivals
quiz.e: The emphasis excludes Rabbi Yehuda's posts-and-beam construction: the Rabbis reject it as a private domain entirely, even regarding the more severe prohibition of throwing an object into the enclosed space.
